title: Dynamic retention profiles with priority-based snapshotting for requests and telemetry
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Implement a flexible retention engine that applies dynamic TTLs across prompts, responses, request logs, and telemetry metrics using priority-based snapshotting rules. The system should support per-tenant overrides, workload-aware sampling, and on-demand evidence bundle generation for audits.
background: Current retention enforcement is route-level and largely static. Customers and compliance teams have requested finer-grained retention controls: different treatment for high-sensitivity prompts vs. generic telemetry, the ability to capture periodic immutable snapshots for audit windows, plus a runtime hook to export evidence bundles. Existing PM work covers retention DSL and UI; engineering must deliver the runtime, storage rules, and export mechanics.
goals: 1) Provide retention tiers (hot/short/archival) mapped to request attributes and tenant policies. 2) Snapshot important traffic (high-priority prompts or policy-matched requests) at configurable intervals for immutable evidence. 3) Allow sampled metrics and logs to be retained at different granularities. 4) Ensure exports contain verifiable hash chains and metadata for legal/audit review.
non_goals: 1) This ticket does not build the Console UI for authoring policies (PM will add). 2) It does not implement KMS/HSM integration for bundle signing (separate security task).
technical_design: - Retention Engine: New microservice 'retentiond' that consumes enriched request events from the event bus and evaluates retention policy rules. - Policy Expression: Reuse RPEL (policy expression language) from PM; retentiond compiles RPEL to evaluation plan at startup. - Snapshotting: For requests tagged 'priority:high' or matching audit rules, retentiond writes a snapshot to an immutable S3 prefix (or internal object store for Private). Snapshots include raw request, response, route metadata, timestamp, and canonicalized policy version. -TTL Enforcement: Short-lived objects get lifecycle tags; a background sweeper reconciles object store and indexes to delete expired blobs. -Sampling: Metrics and request logs support stratified reservoir sampling with percent and time-window parameters. -Evidence Bundles: On-demand bundle builder aggregates snapshots, attaches provenance metadata, computes sha256 per file and an overall manifest with hash chain. -Per-tenant Overrides: Policies can be scoped by tenant id with precedence rules. -Backwards compatibility: For routes without new policies, fall back to existing global TTLs.
data_schema_changes: - Add 'retention_policy_id' and 'policy_version' fields to request events (string). - Add 'snapshot_id' and 'snapshot_reason' tags to object metadata. - Add 'evidence_manifest' schema (flat keys only: manifest_id, created_at, files_count, sha256).
api_changes: - POST /v1/retention/preview (internal) -> returns simulated TTLs for a given sample of request events. - POST /v1/evidence/exports -> start a signed evidence bundle build (async job id). - GET /v1/evidence/exports/{id}/status -> export status and download link. - Admin-only hooks for manual snapshot trigger: POST /v1/retention/snapshot. (All endpoints authenticated and audited.)
acceptance_criteria: Retentiond evaluates policy rules and assigns TTL tags within 5s of event ingestion for >95% of events in load test.
Snapshots for high-priority requests are written and digestable by the bundle builder; manifest sha256 matches concatenated file hashes.
Per-tenant override demonstrates higher-priority TTL for test tenant and does not affect other tenants in integration environment.
Retention sweeper deletes expired keys and associated indexes; end-to-end test verifies object removal and event index reconciliation.
Export API produces a downloadable evidence bundle containing snapshots, manifest, and provenance metadata within SLA for small exports (<1GB).
rollout_plan: 1) Canary deploy retentiond in staging, subscribe to 10% of traffic via routing rule. 2) Validate snapshot and TTL behavior for canary tenants. 3) Gradually ramp to 50% then 100% of non-critical routes while monitoring errors. 4) Run a tenant-scoped test of per-tenant overrides. 5) Coordinate with PM for console toggle and Customer Success for pilot customers.
monitoring_and_alerting: - Metrics: eval_latency_ms, snapshots_written_total, snapshot_errors_total, sweeper_deleted_total, export_job_duration_seconds. - Alerts: eval_latency > 2000ms for 5m; snapshot_errors_total spike > 5 in 1m; export_job_failure_ratio > 1%.
test_plan: - Unit tests for policy compilation and TTL assignment. - Integration test: end-to-end ingestion -> snapshot -> bundle export -> manifest verification. - Load test: 5k events/s with mixed priorities to validate latency and correctness. - Chaos test: simulate object store eventual consistency during sweeper run. - Compliance test: generate audit bundle and perform manual review with Security.
docs_needed: - Confluence design doc with policy precedence and examples. - API docs for preview/export endpoints. - Runbook for snapshot recovery and bundle verification. - Customer-facing KB explaining priority snapshot semantics.
risks_mitigation: - Risk: Snapshot volume could overwhelm object store. Mitigation: cap snapshot rate per tenant and implement backpressure (drop-to-sampled mode) with alerting. - Risk: Export bundles contain sensitive PII. Mitigation: tie export permission to role-based checks and log all export actions. - Risk: Incorrect deletions. Mitigation: sweeper runs in dry-run mode for first two weeks and can be reverted via retention-dry-run flag.
notes: - We chose a separate retentiond service to keep evaluation off the hot request path and make per-tenant scaling straightforward. - There is some overlap with PM's retention simulator; this ticket will integrate that simulator via /preview endpoint rather than reimplementing. - KMS signing will be handled by a follow-up security ticket.
